incident: On 5 September 2026, an unknown person took the complainant's bicycle parked outside the grocery store without his consent.
notes: Classic BNS Section 303 (Theft) case. Moving movable property out of possession without consent.

incident: On 10 August 2026, at around 8 PM, an unknown man stole the complainant's mobile phone while he was standing at the bus stop.
notes: Core theft under Section 303 is supported, but specific sub-clause proviso for property value < 5,000 rupees must be uncertain as value is unstated.

incident: On 12 August 2026, an unknown person stole a cheap plastic watch valued at 800 rupees from the complainant's desk.
notes: Theft under Section 303 with explicit monetary value of 800 rupees (< 5,000 rupees threshold).

incident: On 15 August 2026, two men on a speed motorcycle rode past the complainant and suddenly grabbed her gold chain from her neck with force and sped away.
notes: BNS Section 304 (Snatching): Theft by sudden, quick, or forcible seizure of property worn/carried.

incident: On 20 August 2026, an assailant threatened the victim at knifepoint, stating 'Hand over your wallet immediately or I will stab you', and forcibly took the wallet.
notes: BNS Section 309 (Robbery): Theft accompanied by instant fear of death or hurt caused for that end.

incident: On 22 August 2026, during an argument at a tea stall, the accused raised his fist and charged towards the complainant, creating apprehension that he was about to strike him.
notes: BNS Section 130 (Assault): Making a gesture or preparation causing apprehension of criminal force.

incident: On 25 August 2026, during a altercation over parking, the accused punched the complainant in the face, causing a bloody nose and severe facial pain.
notes: BNS Section 115 (Voluntarily causing hurt): Act done with intention/knowledge of causing bodily pain or hurt.

incident: On 28 August 2026, an unknown man slapped the complainant across the face and immediately grabbed his mobile phone and fled.
notes: BNS Section 134 (Assault/criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried) and BNS Section 303 (Theft).

category: Force used specifically to facilitate theft
incident: On 1 September 2026, a stranger punched the victim in the chest in order to knock him down so he could snatch his leather bag.
notes: Explicit force used to facilitate theft of property carried by victim (Section 134 / Section 304). Section 309 Robbery is uncertain.

incident: On 3 September 2026, the complainant was shoved during a crowded market commotion. A few minutes later, he noticed his wallet was missing from his pocket.
notes: Theft (Section 303) is supported. Criminal force / robbery connection is uncertain due to ambiguous sequence and intent.

incident: On 5 September 2026, a driver drove a motor car at 120 km/h through a crowded market street, zigzagging dangerously and endangering pedestrians, though no person was hit.
notes: BNS Section 281 (Rash driving or riding on a public way endangering human life or safety).

incident: On 7 September 2026, a speeding car collided with a motorcycle from behind on MG Road, causing the motorcyclist to fall and suffer leg fractures and injuries.
notes: BNS Section 281 (Rash driving) and BNS Section 125 (Act endangering life or personal safety of others / causing hurt).

incident: On 8 September 2026, a rashly driven truck hit a pedestrian crossing the road, resulting in the instant death of the pedestrian.
notes: BNS Section 281 (Rash driving) and BNS Section 106 (Causing death by negligence).

incident: On 10 September 2026, the accused physically stood in front of the complainant's doorway and blocked him from leaving his office room, preventing him from moving in that direction.
notes: BNS Section 126 (Wrongful restraint): Voluntarily obstructing a person so as to prevent him from proceeding in any direction.

incident: On 12 September 2026, the accused locked the complainant inside a storage room from the outside for three hours, preventing him from proceeding beyond circumscribed limits.
notes: BNS Section 127 (Wrongful confinement): Wrongfully restraining a person in such a manner as to prevent that person from proceeding beyond certain circumscribed limits.

incident: On 14 September 2026, the accused fraudulently induced the complainant to pay 50,000 rupees by promising a government job with fake employment documents.
notes: BNS Section 318 (Cheating): Deceiving a person and fraudulently/dishonestly inducing delivery of property/money.

incident: On 16 September 2026, the accused threatened the complainant saying 'If you testify in court tomorrow, I will burn down your house and kill your family'.
notes: BNS Section 351 (Criminal intimidation): Threatening another with injury to person, reputation, or property with intent to cause alarm.

incident: On 18 September 2026, the complainant entrusted his laptop to his friend for temporary work use, but the friend dishonestly sold the laptop and kept the money.
notes: BNS Section 316 (Criminal breach of trust): Dishonest misappropriation of property entrusted to a person.

incident: On 20 September 2026, an accountant employed at a private firm dishonestly took 40,000 rupees cash from the office safe in his master's possession.
notes: BNS Section 306 (Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master).

incident: On 22 September 2026, an intruder entered the complainant's residential house during the afternoon and stole jewelry from the bedroom closet.
notes: BNS Section 305 (Theft in a dwelling house). Trespass/house-breaking provisions may be uncertain if entry method is unstated.

incident: On 24 September 2026, a member of a known local gang engaged in systematic street pickpocketing and mobile snatching as part of an organized crime group operation.
notes: BNS Section 112 (Petty organised crime) and BNS Section 304 (Snatching).

incident: On 26 September 2026, a man gave false information to the police officer at the station claiming his neighbor committed a robbery, knowing the statement to be false, intending to cause the officer to use lawful power to annoy the neighbor.
notes: BNS Section 217 (Giving false information to public servant with intent to cause use of lawful power to injury/annoyance).

incident: On 28 September 2026, an accused repeatedly followed a woman online and in person, sending unwanted explicit messages despite her clear refusal.
notes: BNS Section 78 (Stalking): Following a woman and contacting/attempting to contact her despite clear disinterest.

incident: On 30 September 2026, the accused removed and defaced the official serial brand mark stamped on industrial machinery owned by the complainant with intent to cause injury.
notes: BNS Section 346 (Tampering with property mark with intent to cause injury).

incident: On 2 October 2026, after being suddenly slapped without warning, the victim lost self-control under grave and sudden provocation and pushed the aggressor.
notes: BNS Section 136 (Assault or criminal force on grave and sudden provocation).

category: A case where important statutory facts are missing
incident: On 4 October 2026, the complainant reported that something suspicious happened near his vehicle in the parking lot, but could not describe any act, loss, or perpetrator.
notes: No core statutory elements established. Zero supported sections expected.

category: A case designed to trigger a likely retrieval false positive
incident: On 6 October 2026, a car collided with a motorcycle on a city road. The driver stopped immediately and rendered help. The incident involved no ship, boat, vessel, or water navigation.
notes: Designed to test false-positive resistance against BNS Section 282 (Rash navigation of vessel). Only Section 281 is supported.

incident: On 8 October 2026, the complainant found a gold ring lying on a public sidewalk. He picked it up and put it in his pocket without attempting to find the owner.
notes: BNS Section 314 (Dishonest misappropriation of property). Theft under Section 303 is uncertain as initial possession was not taken out of another's active custody.

incident: On 10 October 2026, the accused broke the lock of a residential house at night, entered inside, punched the house owner causing bodily pain, and stole 20,000 rupees cash.
notes: Multi-offence incident: Section 305 (Theft in dwelling house), Section 115 (Hurt), Section 331 (Lurking house-trespass or house-breaking at night).

incident: On 12 October 2026, the complainant and his landlord had a disagreement regarding the monthly rent increase specified in their tenancy lease contract.
notes: Civil tenancy/contractual dispute with no criminal statutory offences established.
